name: Viola
lede: Viola is a muted violet-purple from a 1930 American color dictionary, named with the Italian word for the violet.

sections.title: Name and sources
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary gives viola plate 42, block H7, and first records it in 1923 [1]. Who first used it as a color is undocumented. The word also names the plant genus *Viola*, and Baty's nineteenth-century palette lists the sweet-scented violet, *Viola odorata*, among its blues and purples [2]. A flower named viola also appears in Jarman's book, but it is not about this color [3].

On screen it is close to [[faded-purple]] and [[amethyst]], 9.4 units apart, and a little duller than [[violet]] [1]. A paler relative is [[lilac]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 museum paintings, only 2 contain this color over at least five per cent of the canvas, Signac's *Woman with a Parasol* of 1893 and Dupuis's Le Havre embankment of 1908 [4]. Both are French, and both read as a shadow color [4]. Two paintings is too few to say more. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [4].
